questions.answer: Hmmm be prepared to have an open mind and maybe be vocal about what your level of hygiene is since it prob wont be the same as people with other backgrounds

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its never easy as you tend to overthink about every small thing but in regards to the process the try to make it as streamline as possible

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In short you had to registrer for classes and that you were going to physically be there

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a very good support team with a bunch of very helpful staff that could solve a lot of your problems big or small

questions.answer: very successful however, i did change one of my courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're ever in doubt go the library and ask HiQ for support

questions.answer: So much! they had almost every type of interest

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: maybe join a running club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: GO travel!! Brisbane is only 2 hours away from some very iconic destinations! both accessable by car or public transport which can be very cheap if you registrer for the student discount

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy as aussies share a lot of the same humor and vibe as europeans

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go talk to them! sit next to them! introduce yourself! everybody is usually just a desperate to make a friend as you are

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The school terms were very new to me and with a mix of aussie slang could be a bit confusing in the beginning

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the laid back attitude and the understated approach to everything

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Talk to new people - it gets easier every time
2. Dont be afraid to ask and make plans 
3. Do things you would never do at home - this is the best place to grow as person

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: have fun and embrace change and challenges

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the personal growth

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: sometimes to understand the specific type of structure to some assignments

questions.answer: Yes
